title: Philosophy of mind
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Study the mind-body problem and its main answers (substance and property dualism, behaviorism, the identity theory, functionalism and eliminativism), the Turing test and the Chinese room, intentionality, mental causation, consciousness and the hard problem, the knowledge and zombie arguments, and personal identity and the self.

weeks.1: The mind-body problem and Cartesian dualism
weeks.5: Machines and minds: the Turing test
weeks.8: Mental causation and the exclusion problem
weeks.10: The knowledge argument and the zombie argument

blocks.deliverable: Reconstruct Descartes's argument for dualism and one objection.
Explain multiple realizability with three examples.
Evaluate the systems reply to the Chinese room.
Week 7 midterm; reconstruct the exclusion argument.
Reconstruct the knowledge argument and the ability reply.
Write a three-page essay on the hard problem.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Philosophy of mind paper: write a 2,500-word paper defending an answer to one question (can physicalism explain consciousness, could a machine think, or is mental causation a problem for nonreductive physicalism), reconstructing the strongest opposing argument and replying to it.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
